nodes.label: Degree of regularity d_reg (Bardet-Faugere-Salvy)
nodes.statement: For F in k[x_1..x_n] with (F^top)_d = R_d for d >> 0, d_reg(F) = min{d : (F^top)_d = R_d}, where F^top are the highest-degree homogeneous parts; equivalently the index of regularity of (F^top), and reg(F^top) (CG 2020 Proposition 2). If no such d exists d_reg is undefined (+infinity).
nodes.scope: BFS definition. Distinct from the Dubois-Gama/Ding-Schmidt 'degree of regularity' (a first-fall degree, DEF-GB-DS-DEGREE-OF-REGULARITY) and from the HKYY usage 'largest degree seen in a DRL Groebner basis computation' (a solving degree). Statements quoting 'degree of regularity' must say which one.
non_implications: Not a bound on the solving degree by definition (see CEX-GB-BDDGMT-EX24, MEAS-GB-CG-SUMMATION-SD-GT-DREG)

nodes.label: Dubois-Gama / Ding-Schmidt degree of regularity (= first fall degree)
nodes.statement: For quadratic f_1..f_r in B = F_q[x]/(x_1^q..x_n^q), delta_reg(F) = min{d >= 2 : Syz(F^top)_{d-2}/Triv(F^top)_{d-2} != 0}, trivial syzygies being Koszul syzygies and f_i^(q-1) e_i; CG 2021 Definition 1.3 calls the general version the first fall degree d_ff. Dubois-Gama work in F_q[x]/(x_i^q - x_i).
nodes.scope: This is the quantity HFE and summation-polynomial first-fall analyses bound. CG 2020 states it knows no result relating delta_reg to the BFS d_reg despite the shared name.

nodes.label: Semi-regular and cryptographic semi-regular sequences
nodes.statement: Pardue: homogeneous f_1..f_m is semi-regular if each f_i acts with maximal rank in every degree on R/(f_1..f_{i-1}); equivalently its Hilbert series is [prod_i (1-z^{d_i})/(1-z)^n] (truncated at the first non-positive coefficient) for every prefix. BFS 'cryptographic semi-regular' requires only HS_{R/(f_1..f_m)}(z) = [prod_{i=1}^m (1-z^{d_i})/(1-z)^n]; every semi-regular sequence is cryptographic semi-regular, not conversely. For m <= n semi-regular = regular. For m > n the ideal is Artinian and d_reg is the first degree where the series coefficient is non-positive.
nodes.scope: Homogeneous systems; an affine system is called (cryptographic) semi-regular via F^top (BFS) or via F^h (Bigdeli et al. Definition 3.6). The two affine conventions give different predicted degrees.
source_locations: Bigdeli et al. 2021, Definitions 1.8, 1.11, 3.6, Proposition 1.10, Remark 1.12

nodes.label: Semi-regular sequences over F_2 (Boolean, field equations)
nodes.statement: Over F_2 with field equations, work in B(n) = F_2[x]/(x_1^2..x_n^2); a homogeneous sequence is semi-regular over F_2 if (I != B(n) and) every relation g_i f_i = 0 in B/(f_1..f_{i-1}) of degree < index of regularity has g_i in (f_1..f_i) (Frobenius-adjusted). Its Hilbert series is [(1+z)^n / prod_i (1+z^{d_i})]_+, and the index of regularity is at most n+1.
nodes.scope: This is the model behind 'semi-regular degree' estimates for Boolean Weil-descent systems (binary summation-polynomial descents add x_i^2 + x_i).

cited_by.note: column D_sr: the semi-regular degree of a Boolean system with the same equation degrees, used as the reference bound
matrix-F5 criterion in the BFS form used to analyse semi-regular systems

nodes.label: Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and generic coordinates
nodes.statement: reg(I) for homogeneous I is read off the graded minimal free resolution (CG 2020 Definition 10). A homogeneous J is in generic coordinates (Bayer-Stillman) if the last variable is a non-zero-divisor on S/J^sat; then reg(J) = reg(in_DRL(J)) (Bayer-Stillman Thm 2.4, CG 2020 Theorem 8). For a homogenized affine system, J = (F^h) is in generic coordinates iff t is not a zero divisor modulo J^sat.
nodes.scope: In positive characteristic maxGBdeg_DRL(J) <= reg(in_DRL(J)) may be strict (CG 2020 Remark 11: (x^p, y^p) has maxGBdeg p, reg 2p-1).

nodes.label: Macaulay-matrix Groebner cost up to degree D
nodes.statement: For homogeneous f_1..f_m in k[x_1..x_n], computing a Groebner basis for a graded order up to degree D costs O(m D binom(n+D-1, D)^omega) field operations as D -> infinity (omega the matrix-multiplication exponent). Any degree invariant becomes a cost only through this (or the affine M_{<=d} analogue).
nodes.scope: Upper bound in field operations for linear-algebra-based algorithms (Lazard, XL, F4/F5 in matrix form); D must be a degree at which the computation actually stops, i.e. a solving degree, not a first fall degree.
assumptions: Homogeneous input (affine input via homogenization or M_{<=d})

nodes.label: Lazard/Macaulay bound for regular systems
nodes.statement: For a homogeneous system with variables in simultaneous Noether position (e.g. a regular sequence after a generic linear change of coordinates over an infinite field), every element of the reduced grevlex Groebner basis has degree <= sum_{i}(d_i - 1) + 1; affine version (CG 2020 Corollary 2, Lazard Thm 2): if |Z_+(F^h)| < infinity and (F^h) is in generic coordinates, sd_DRL(F) <= d_1+..+d_l - l + 1 with l = min(n+1, r), d_1 >= d_2 >= ...; in particular (n+1)(d-1)+1 for r > n.
nodes.scope: Without a generic change of coordinates the bound does not hold in general (Mayr-Meyer observation cited by BFS). It is linear in n and d, so a Macaulay-bound cost is exponential in n for any nontrivial d.
assumptions: Simultaneous Noether position or generic coordinates
Finitely many projective solutions of F^h (affine form)

nodes.label: Matrix-F5 complexity for regular systems (BFS Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: For homogeneous f_1..f_m of identical degree delta >= 2 in n variables, m = n - l, l >= 0, with variables in simultaneous Noether position, matrix-F5 computes a grevlex Groebner basis in B(delta)^n n (A(delta,l) + O(1/n)) operations as n -> infinity (l, delta = O(1)), with delta^3 <= B(delta) <= 3 delta^3 (B(2)^n = 2^{4.29 n}); for regular sequences all F5 matrices have full rank (no reduction to zero, Theorem 9).
nodes.scope: Regular (m <= n) systems only; the overdetermined semi-regular case is the thesis/BFSY asymptotics (THM-GB-BFS-DREG-ASYMPTOTICS). Affine systems need simultaneous Noether position of F^top.

cited_by.note: implements the matrix-F5 criterion in BFS form over F_2

nodes.label: Asymptotic degree of regularity of semi-regular sequences
nodes.statement: For a semi-regular sequence of n+k equations of degrees d_i in n variables, D_reg = sum (d_i-1)/2 - alpha_k sqrt(sum (d_i^2-1)/6) + O(1) (alpha_k the largest root of the k-th Hermite polynomial); for alpha n quadratic equations (alpha > 1 fixed), D_reg = (alpha - 1/2 - sqrt(alpha(alpha-1))) n + O(n^{1/3}) with an Airy-root correction; over F_2 with alpha n quadratic equations, D_reg ~ (-alpha + 1/2 + (1/2) sqrt(2 alpha^2 - 10 alpha - 1 + 2(alpha+2) sqrt(alpha(alpha+2)))) n; for n quadratic equations over F_2, D_reg = 0.0900 n + 1.00 n^{1/3} - 1.58 + O(n^{-1/3}).
nodes.scope: Rigorous asymptotics of the Hilbert-series index for sequences that ARE semi-regular. Using it for a concrete system needs that system to be semi-regular (HEUR-GB-SEMIREG-ASSUMPTION) and needs d_reg to control the solving degree (it does only up to +1 for mutant algorithms, THM-GB-SALIZZONI-SD-LE-DREG-PLUS-1, or up to 2d_reg-2 for two-phase algorithms, THM-GB-SEMAEV-TENTI-2DREG).
assumptions: The input sequence is semi-regular (over K or over F_2)

nodes.label: Froberg's conjecture (generic Hilbert series)
nodes.statement: Over an infinite field, a generic sequence of homogeneous forms of degrees d_1..d_m in n variables has Hilbert series [prod (1-z^{d_i})/(1-z)^n]_+; equivalently (Pardue) generic sequences are semi-regular. Proved for m <= n, n = 2, n = 3 (infinite field), m = n+1 in characteristic 0, and small quadratic/cubic cases (n <= 11 for d=2, n <= 8 for d=3 at thesis time).
nodes.scope: Open in general. Even if true it is a statement about infinite fields and Zariski-generic coefficients; over a finite field 'generic' is not 'almost all' (Bigdeli et al. Section 1.2).
source_locations: Bigdeli et al. 2021, discussion after Remark 1.9 (Pardue Conjecture B)

nodes.label: BFS Conjecture 2: almost all F_2 sequences are semi-regular
nodes.statement: For any (n, m, d_1..d_m), the proportion of semi-regular sequences over F_2 among systems of m equations of degrees d_i in n variables tends to 1 as n -> infinity (BFS RR-5049 Conjecture 2; Bardet's thesis states the genericity conjecture in Section 5.2 with m allowed to depend on n and uses it to read semi-regular bounds as average-case complexity for cryptographic systems).
nodes.scope: Refuted for fixed (m, d_1..d_m) by Hodges-Molina-Schlather Theorem 7.14 (the proportion tends to 0). The thesis variant with m growing with n is not covered by that theorem and is open (HMS Conjecture 4 is a corrected form).
source_locations: BFS RR-5049, Conjecture 2 (quoted in HMS 2017 p. 6)
non_implications: Does not say random F_2 systems with m proportional to n fail to be semi-regular
Does not invalidate the asymptotic formulas for sequences that are semi-regular

nodes.label: Hodges-Molina-Schlather: no semi-regular sequences of fixed type for large n
nodes.statement: Over F_2 (algebra B(n) = F_2[x]/(x_i^2)): (Thm 4.10) there are no semi-regular elements of degree d >= 2 when n > 3d; (Thm 4.11) none of degree 2 for n >= 7; (Thm 7.14) for a fixed type d = (d_1..d_m) with some d_j >= 2 there is N such that for all n >= N no semi-regular sequence of type d exists. The proof uses Hodges-Petit-Schlather's first fall bound D_ff(lambda) <= (s+d+2)/2 for lambda of degree d and rank s (HMS Thm 4.7) and the fact that index > D_ff forbids semi-regularity (Thm 4.8).
nodes.scope: Fixed number of equations, n -> infinity. Theorem 6.4 proves a trivial-sense version of 'proportion -> 1' over all homogeneous subsets, which HMS say does not capture the cryptographic conjecture.
assumptions: Field F_2 with field equations (Boolean algebra B(n))

nodes.label: Semi-regularity assumption: cryptographic systems behave like semi-regular ones and d_reg sets the cost
nodes.statement: Estimates of the form 'cost = Macaulay/F5 cost at D = d_reg of a semi-regular system with the same (n, m, d_i)' assume (a) the concrete system (or its F^top, or F^h) is semi-regular and (b) the computation stops at or near that d_reg.
nodes.scope: Both halves fail in published examples: (a) is false for fixed-size Boolean systems at large n (HMS Thm 7.14) and for structured systems such as HFE; (b) fails for affine systems even when F^top is semi-regular (Bigdeli et al. Ex. 2.4: sd = 5 > 4 = d_reg) and for index-calculus summation systems (CG 2020 Ex. 12, 13). Rigorous replacements: sd <= d_reg + 1 for mutant algorithms (Salizzoni), sd <= reg(F^h) in generic coordinates (CG), sd <= 2d_reg - 2 for two-phase algorithms (Semaev-Tenti; Kudo-Yokoyama without field equations).
assumptions: Input is semi-regular in the convention used (F^top or F^h)
failure_modes: Structured (non-random) systems such as HFE or summation descents are not semi-regular
Affine degree falls push the solving degree above d_reg(F^top)
d_reg undefined because F^top has positive-dimensional zero set
Fixed-m Boolean systems at large n are never semi-regular

cited_by.note: compares the degree reached against the semi-regular degree D_sr

nodes.label: maxGBdeg <= d_reg, but not sd <= d_reg (CG 2020 Remark 15)
nodes.statement: If (F^top)_d = R_d for d >> 0 and tau is degree-compatible, every element of the reduced tau-Groebner basis of (F) has degree <= d_reg(F). This inequality 'does not yield a bound on the solving degree' (CG 2020, after Remark 15).
nodes.scope: Rigorous for maxGBdeg only; solving degree can exceed it (Example 9: sd = 3 > maxGBdeg = 2; Examples 12, 13).

nodes.label: Solving degree <= Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity (CG 2020 Thms 7, 9, 10)
nodes.statement: With DRL and t the smallest variable: maxGBdeg(F^h) = sd(F^h) >= sd(F) >= maxGBdeg(F) = maxGBdeg(I^h) = sd(I^h) (Theorem 7). If (F^h) (or (F) when homogeneous) is in generic coordinates over k, then sd_DRL(F) <= reg(F^h) (Theorems 9, 10); the bound is often an equality.
nodes.scope: Rigorous. The generic-coordinates hypothesis is the crux; for zero-dimensional affine F it is equivalent to d_reg(F) < infinity (Steiner Cor. 3.5), and it holds automatically when F contains the field equations (CG 2020 Theorem 11). Solving degree here is the plain Macaulay-matrix one (Definition 6), an upper bound on mutant variants.
source_locations: Caminata-Gorla 2020, Theorem 7, Theorem 9, Theorem 10, Remark 12 ([CG17] Theorems 3.22/3.23)

nodes.label: Field equations force generic coordinates and a Macaulay bound (CG 2020 Thm 11)
nodes.statement: If F over a field of characteristic p contains x_i^q - x_i for all i (or the cyclic fake-Weil-descent equations x_1^q - x_2, ..., x_n^q - x_1), then (F^h) is in generic coordinates over the algebraic closure and sd_DRL(F) <= d_1+..+d_l - l + 1 (l = min(n+1, r)); for r > n and d = d_1, sd_DRL(F) <= (n+1)(d-1)+1.
nodes.scope: Rigorous but coarse: with field equations of degree q the bound is at least about n(q-1), i.e. linear in the number of descended variables, so it gives exponential-in-n cost for Weil-descent systems. Remark 13: any system containing x_i^{d_i} + lower terms for each i is in generic coordinates.
assumptions: Field equations (or their fake Weil descent) included

nodes.label: CG 2020 Ex. 12: index-calculus summation systems have sd = 5 > d_reg = 4
nodes.statement: For the Gaudry-style relation-collection systems of [BG18] with n = 3 (three affine cubic equations in two variables), on 150,000 random cryptographic-size instances (3 primes q, 5 curves each, 10,000 points per curve): (F^top)_d = R_d for d >> 0 and sd_DRL(F) = reg(F^h) = 5 > 4 = d_reg(F) = i_reg(F^top). Computed by G. Bianco in Magma.
nodes.scope: Prime-field-extension (F_{q^3}) decomposition systems of the Gaudry/Diem type. A published computation, not a proof; shows the BFS degree of regularity under-predicts the solving degree on ECDLP systems while reg(F^h) matches it.
assumptions: Magma computation as reported (published computational result, not a proof)

nodes.label: CG 2020 Ex. 13: summation systems with d_reg undefined, i_reg(F^top) = 8 vs sd = 15
nodes.statement: For the [GM15] index-calculus relation systems with n = 3 (three affine equations of degrees 7, 7, 8 in two variables), on 150,000 random cryptographic-size instances: sd_DRL(F) = reg(F^h) = 15 while (F^top)_d != R_d for all d (d_reg undefined although |Z(F)| is finite) and i_reg(F^top) = 8.
nodes.scope: Shows that substituting i_reg(F^top) for an undefined d_reg understates the solving degree by almost a factor 2 on an ECDLP system. By Steiner Cor. 3.5 such zero-dimensional F has F^h NOT in generic coordinates, so the equality sd = reg(F^h) here is observed, not guaranteed by CG Theorem 10.
assumptions: Magma computation as reported (published computational result, not a proof)

nodes.label: Bigdeli et al. Ex. 2.4: semi-regular F^top yet sd = d_reg + 1
nodes.statement: F = {x^4 - 1, x^2 y - x^2, y^2 - 1} over F_7: (F^top) = (x^4, x^2 y, y^2) is generated by a cryptographic semi-regular sequence and d_reg(F) = 4, the reduced DRL basis is {y - 1, x^4 - 1}, and sd(F) = 5 > 4 = d_reg(F).
nodes.scope: Exact small example. Together with Salizzoni Thm 1.1 it shows the +1 is attained even when F^top is semi-regular.

nodes.label: Bigdeli et al. Ex. 2.2-2.3: sd far above d_reg with field equations
nodes.statement: Over F_7 with field equations included (radical ideals): products of f_1 = x^5+y^5+z^5-1, f_2 = x^3+y^3+z^2-1, f_3 = y^6-1, f_4 = z^6-1 give solv.deg = 24 > 15 = d_reg (Ex. 2.2); products of pairs from {f_1, f_2, x^7-x, y^7-y, z^7-z} give 21 > 13 = d_reg (Ex. 2.3). The paper states that the input degrees (18, resp. 14) do not account for the gap.
nodes.scope: Magma 'largest step degree' used as a proxy for the solving degree. Bigdeli et al. state they found no proof in the literature that d_reg bounds the solving degree and that these examples show it does not.
assumptions: Magma largest step degree as proxy for sd
source_locations: Bigdeli et al. 2021, Examples 2.2 and 2.3, and the paragraph after Definition 2.1

nodes.label: Regularity-based solving-degree bounds for semi-regular systems (Bigdeli et al.)
nodes.statement: For a homogeneous cryptographic semi-regular sequence of n+1 forms in n variables, maxGBdeg(I) <= floor((d_1+..+d_{n+1}-n-1)/2) + 1 (Theorem 3.2; n+1 quadrics: floor((n+1)/2)+1; cubics: n+2), and the same bounds sd if I is in generic coordinates; explicit r(m,n) for m = n+2..n+5 quadrics (Theorem 3.4) and m >= n+2 cubics (Thm 3.11: n+3). Inhomogeneous systems whose F^h is cryptographic semi-regular inherit these bounds (Theorems 3.7, 3.8, 3.10); e.g. m = n+1 affine quadrics give sd <= n+2. Under the Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture, Theorem 4.4 gives sharper bounds for quadratic systems containing a regular sequence of length n.
nodes.scope: Rigorous given semi-regularity of F^h and generic coordinates; the semi-regularity itself is the heuristic input over finite fields. Corollary 2.6: if F contains the field equations and t is a non-zero-divisor modulo (F^h), sd(F) <= d_reg(F) - but t usually divides zero.
assumptions: (F^h) in generic coordinates (or field equations included)
source_locations: Bigdeli et al. 2021, Theorems 2.5, 3.1, 3.2, 3.4, 3.7, 3.8, 3.10, 3.11; Corollary 2.6; Theorem 4.4 (conditional on Conjecture 4.3)

nodes.label: Bigdeli et al. Ex. 3.9: Joux-Vitse decomposition systems are cryptographic semi-regular
nodes.statement: Running Joux-Vitse-style point decomposition over F_{q^n}, q a large prime, n in {3,4,5} (decomposing into n-1 factor-base points), almost all of the resulting overdetermined systems of n equations in n-1 variables were inhomogeneous cryptographic semi-regular; their homogenizations are regular sequences of n forms in n variables, so sd <= d_1+..+d_n - (n-1).
nodes.scope: Python experiment, extension degree n <= 5, large-prime base field; says nothing about binary fields or growing n. Gives the rigorous bound for instances that are verified semi-regular, which is a Macaulay-type bound (linear in the summation-polynomial degrees 2^{n-2}, so exponential in n).

nodes.label: Salizzoni: sd <= d_reg + 1 (mutant solving degree), optimal
nodes.statement: If max deg(f_i) <= d_reg(F) < infinity and sigma is degree-compatible, then sd_sigma(F) <= d_reg(F) + 1, where sd is defined through the spaces V_{F,d} (mutant-style, equal to the Macaulay-with-reinsertion degree by GMP Theorem 1). In general sd_sigma(F) <= max{d_reg(F)+1, deg f_1, .., deg f_k} (Proposition 3.10). The bound is attained for every d > 1 (Example 3.9).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. Applies to MutantXL/MXL2-type and degree-by-degree reinsertion algorithms; the plain Macaulay solving degree of CG 2020 (no reinsertion) can be larger. Requires d_reg finite.
assumptions: Solving degree in the V_{F,d} (reinsertion) sense

nodes.label: Salizzoni: last-fall bound, improved Macaulay bound, O((n+1)^{4(d+1)}) cost
nodes.statement: Corollary 3.11: d_lastfall(F) <= max{d_reg(F)+1, deg f_1..deg f_k}. Corollary 3.12: if d_reg(F) < infinity (so k >= n) and d_1 >= .. >= d_k, sd_sigma(F) <= d_1+..+d_n - n + 2 (depends on n, not n+1, degrees). Proposition 3.13: if deg f_i <= d_reg(F) = d, a Groebner basis is found in O((n+1)^{4(d+1)}) field operations.
nodes.scope: Rigorous. The cost bound is polynomial in n for bounded d_reg, which is exactly what a first-fall-style estimate would need, but only for the BFS d_reg (top-degree regularity), not for a first fall degree.
nodes.formula: Lfd(F) <= max{d_reg+1, deg F}; cost O((n+1)^{4(d_reg+1)})

nodes.label: Salizzoni Ex. 3.9: sd = last fall = d_reg + 1
nodes.statement: For k > 1, F_k = {x^k + y, y^k + x, xy}: F^top = {x^k, y^k, xy}, so d_reg(F_k) = k; {x, y} is the reduced Groebner basis for every order; x, y are not in V_{F,k} but lie in V_{F,k+1}; hence sd_sigma(F_k) = k + 1 = d_reg + 1 for every degree-compatible sigma. Since maxGBdeg = 1, Caminata-Gorla 2021 Theorem 3.1 gives d_lastfall(F_k) = k + 1 > d_reg(F_k).
nodes.scope: The sd value is Salizzoni's; the last-fall value follows immediately from sd = max{Lfd, maxGBdeg} (THM-CG-SOLVING-DEGREE) and is recorded here as that one-line consequence. It contradicts the sentence in Salizzoni's own introduction that 'the last fall degree is always bounded from above by the degree of regularity' when degree of regularity is read as BFS d_reg; his Corollary 3.11 correctly carries the +1.

formal.notes: Small enough (k = 2: three polynomials in two variables) for a decide-style Lean or native exact check of x, y not in V_{F,2} and in V_{F,3}.

nodes.label: 'Last fall degree is always bounded by the degree of regularity' (HKY/HKYY, repeated by Huang 2021/2023)
nodes.statement: HKYY state that the last fall degree 'is always bounded by the degree of regularity' (Prop. 2.6 ii: d_F <= c for any c with a degree-refining Groebner basis inside V_{F,c}), where their 'degree of regularity' is the largest degree seen in a DRL Groebner basis computation, i.e. a solving degree. In that reading the claim is true and equals GMP Theorem 1 (sd >= d_lastfall).
nodes.scope: Reading-sensitive. Under the BFS d_reg (DEF-GB-DEGREE-OF-REGULARITY) it is false: Salizzoni Example 3.9 has d_lastfall = d_reg + 1; the correct BFS-reading statement is d_lastfall <= max{d_reg+1, deg F} (Salizzoni Cor. 3.11). Huang 2021 and 2023 repeat the sentence without stating which degree of regularity is meant.
assumptions: 'degree of regularity' = largest degree reached in a DRL computation (solving degree)
failure_modes: Citing it with BFS d_reg substituted understates the last fall degree by one

nodes.label: GMP Thm 1: Macaulay-with-reinsertion spaces equal V_{E,d}; sd >= last fall
nodes.statement: For a degree-compatible order, the row space W_d produced by Gaussian elimination with reinsertion in degree <= d equals V_{E,d} for all d, and sd_sigma(E) >= d_E (last fall degree). Strict inequality occurs (Example 1: a single polynomial g has sd = deg g, d_E = 0). For lex the conclusion fails (Example 2: E = {X0 - X0 X2^{d-1}, X1 - X2^d}, sd = d < d+1 <= d_E).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. This is the 'easy half' of Caminata-Gorla 2021 Theorem 3.1 and the equivalence that makes the V_{F,d} definition of solving degree (used by Salizzoni) match the Macaulay one with reinsertion.

nodes.label: GMP Thm 4 / Ex. 3: solving degree is coordinate-invariant only with a simple zero
nodes.statement: If E has a single solution of multiplicity one over the algebraic closure, sd_sigma(E) = min{e : dim(V_{E,e} intersect S_{<=1}) >= n} and is independent of affine coordinate changes and of the degree-compatible order. Without that hypothesis it can change: E = {X0^2, X1^2} over F_3 has sd = 2, but after X1 -> X0 + X1 the solving degree is 3.
nodes.scope: Rigorous. ECDLP decomposition systems with factor-base subspaces typically have zero or several solutions, so measured solving degrees depend on the chosen basis of the factor-base subspace and on coordinates.
assumptions: Simple zero (radical ideal with exactly one solution)

nodes.label: GMP: rigorous solving-degree and last-fall bounds for HFE-type Weil descents
nodes.statement: Theorem 5: for k of size q^n and F = {f}, d = deg f, sd_DRL(F^f) <= deg(f) + (q-1)n <= (q-1)(floor(log_q d) + 1 + n) (fake Weil descent with field equations); for HFE-shaped f, sd_DRL <= (q-1)n + 2. Theorem 11: for F in k[X] \ k with d minimal as stated, the last fall degree of the Weil descent system with field equations is <= (q-1) ceil(log_q(d)+1) + 1 (Example 5: bound 6 attained as solving degree 6 in Magma).
nodes.scope: Univariate (HFE) systems. The solving-degree bound grows linearly in n; the last-fall bound is n-independent but last fall alone bounds cost only through Theorem 3.1 together with max GB degree (or via HKYY's solving algorithm). Improves HKYY Theorem 4.5 / HKY15 Theorem 1 by about a factor 2.
source_locations: Gorla-Mueller-Petit 2022, Theorem 5, Lemma 8, Proposition 9, Theorem 11, Example 5

nodes.label: CG 2021 Sec. 4: first fall degree is incomparable with sd, last fall, d_reg, reg
nodes.statement: Explicit systems over F_q show every order is possible and gaps can be arbitrarily large: Ex. 4.1 d_ff = sd = d_F = 3 < q-1 = d_reg < q = reg(F^h); Ex. 4.2 (field equations effectively included) d_ff = d_F = 3 < q-1 = sd < 2q-2 = d_reg; Ex. 4.3 d_F = 0 < 2 = sd < reg(F^h) = d_reg = 3 < q = d_ff; Ex. 4.4 d_ff = 3 < 2q-1 = sd = d_F.
nodes.scope: Rigorous counterexamples. CG name two causes: syzygies of very different degrees make d_ff much smaller than sd (Ex. 4.2, 4.4); ignoring trivial syzygies can make d_ff artificially large (Ex. 4.3). Adding field equations does not remove the gaps.
non_implications: Does not compute any summation-polynomial instance

nodes.label: CG 2021 Ex. 2.4: last fall degree cannot be found by stopping at the first stabilisation
nodes.statement: Although d_F = min{d : V_{F,e} = V_{F,e+1} intersect R_{<=e} for all e >= d}, the set of d with V_{F,d} = V_{F,d+1} intersect R_{<=d} can contain smaller values: for F = {x^2-x, xy-1, w^6-w, w^5 z^5-1} (char 0 or large) the stabilisation holds at d = 0, 1 and fails at d = 2; and V_{F,d} = (F)_{<=d} is strictly stronger than stabilisation (Proposition 2.3).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. Methodological: an experiment that reports 'last fall degree' as the first degree after which nothing new falls, observed for a few degrees, can under-report it.

nodes.label: CG 2021 Thm 5.3: d_reg(F) <= reg(F^h)
nodes.statement: If (F^top)_d = R_d for d >> 0 then d_reg(F) <= reg(F^h).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. With CG 2020 Theorem 10 this sandwiches the regularity bound above d_reg: d_reg is never a larger (safer) estimate than reg(F^h).

nodes.label: Semaev-Tenti: two-phase solving degree <= 2 d_reg - 2 with field equations
nodes.statement: For F = {f_1..f_r, x_1^q - x_1, .., x_n^q - x_n} over F_q with d_reg(F) >= max{q, deg f_i}, sd(F) <= 2 d_reg(F) - 2 (CG 2021 Theorem 5.2 restatement). Kudo-Yokoyama restate it as: there is a two-phase Buchberger-like algorithm with sd <= 2D - 1, and <= 2D - 2 in the strict sense, D = d_reg(F^top). The same paper gives a probabilistic upper bound on d_reg for sufficiently overdetermined random systems of forms over any finite field, holding with probability tending to 1.
nodes.scope: Not read; two secondary restatements differ in the constant and in which algorithm the solving degree refers to; CG 2021 notes the Semaev-Tenti solving degree is defined in F_q[x]/(x^q - x) and may differ from theirs.
source_locations: Semaev-Tenti 2021, Theorem 2.1 (via Caminata-Gorla 2021 Theorem 5.2 and Kudo-Yokoyama Theorem 2.2.5)
Tenti PhD thesis (Bergen 2019), Theorem 3.65 and Corollary 3.67

nodes.label: Kudo-Yokoyama: affine semi-regular degree bounds without field equations
nodes.statement: Theorem 1: (1) if m > n, n+1 <= ... ordering as stated and (f_1^top..f_n^top) is regular, maxGBdeg(F^h) <= d_1+..+d_n + d_m - n; (2) with D = d_reg(F^top) and s the saturation exponent ((F^h):y^s = (F^h):y^infinity), maxGBdeg(F^h) <= D + s - 1. Theorem 2: if F^top is cryptographic semi-regular, before the step degree reaches D the computations for F^top, F^h and F correspond step by step (no degree fall occurs); the first degree fall happens exactly at the y-injectivity threshold d_inj >= D; with the sugar strategy and D >= max deg f, the algorithmic solving degree is <= 2D - 1 (2D - 2 strictly after inter-reduction).
nodes.scope: Rigorous, arbitrary field, no field equations. The y-torsion exponent s is exactly the quantity the BFS heuristic ignores; when (F^h) is y-saturated (s = 1) maxGBdeg(F^h) <= D.

nodes.label: Steiner Cor. 3.5: generic coordinates iff finite d_reg (zero-dimensional)
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, for F with (F) != (1) and dim (F) = 0: F^hom is in generic coordinates iff d_reg(F) < infinity (iff dim(F^top) = 0). Corollary 3.3: every DRL Groebner basis G of a zero-dimensional (F) has (G^hom) in generic coordinates.
nodes.scope: Rigorous. Consequence for ECDLP: a zero-dimensional decomposition system with undefined d_reg (CG 2020 Example 13) is not in generic coordinates, so CG's sd <= reg(F^h) is not available for it as a theorem.

nodes.label: Caminata-Ceria-Gorla: regularity and solving degree of Weil restrictions grow linearly in n
nodes.statement: For a degree-n Galois extension k -> K and homogeneous I in K[x_1..x_m]: reg(Weil(I)) = n reg(I) - n + 1, HS_{Weil(I)} = HS_I^n, dimensions and projective dimensions multiply by n (Theorem 3.3); d_reg(Weil(F)) = n d_reg(F) - n + 1 when (F^top)_d = R_d (Cor. 3.4, Prop. 4.13). For affine F with t a non-zero-divisor mod (F^h) and finitely many projective solutions, sd(Weil(F)) <= n reg(F^h) - n + 1 (Thm 4.7); with the field equations of F_{q^n} and of F_q added, sd(Weil(F) U {x_ij^q - x_ij}) <= n reg(F^h) - n + 1 (Cor. 4.12); complete intersections give n(d_1+..+d_r) - nr + 1 (Cor. 4.10).
nodes.scope: Rigorous upper bounds that grow linearly with the extension degree n, and the d_reg identity is exact: under the BFS invariant, a Weil restriction of a system with d_reg >= 2 has d_reg growing linearly in n, not bounded. Covers full Weil restriction of F; a factor-base subspace constraint (x_i in V) is not part of their setting.
assumptions: Finitely many projective solutions of F^h (Thm 4.7)
source_locations: Caminata-Ceria-Gorla 2023, Theorem 3.3, Corollary 3.4, Theorem 4.5, Theorem 4.7, Corollaries 4.9, 4.10, 4.12, Proposition 4.13
nodes.formula: reg(Weil(I)) = n reg(I) - n + 1; d_reg(Weil(F)) = n d_reg(F) - n + 1

nodes.label: Huang 2021: last fall of Weil descent vs original, non-zero-dimensional
nodes.statement: For F over k = F_{q^n}, with F_1 = F plus the Frobenius-chain equations X_i^q - Y_i1, .., Y_i,n-1^q - X_i and F_1' the Weil descent with field equations of k' = F_q: max(d_{F_1}, q deg F) = max(d_{F_1'}, q deg F) (Theorem 1.1). For k'-linearized F reducible for a tau-invariant subspace W, the last fall degree of F-bar U Q-bar is <= (q-1)m + 1 and a basis of Z_W(F) is found in time (n'm)^{O(q)} (Theorem 2.5); for linearized F of degree q^c reducible for k, d_{F_1'} <= max((q-1)m+1, qd) (Theorem 2.6).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. Transfers the problem to bounding d_{F_1} over K, which is not bounded by the paper for general (e.g. summation) F; the explicit bounds are for linearized polynomials only. The factor-base membership x in V is itself a linearized condition, so Theorems 2.5-2.6 bound that part alone, not the summation polynomial.

nodes.label: Huang 2023: last fall degree of semi-local systems in terms of solution count
nodes.statement: If G = mu o F o lambda is c-semi-local, each local block radical with last fall <= c', and |Z(G)| = s (over the algebraic closure), then d_G <= s + c' ceil(log_2 s) and Z(G) is found in time n^{O(c')} + s^{O(c log s)} (Theorem 3.1); Theorem 3.2 bounds the last fall degree of G with field equations by O(Delta p) (one rational point) or O(max(Delta p, s_0 p, s_0 log s_0)), Delta = max(|Z(F_i)|, d_{F_i}).
nodes.scope: Rigorous. Requires zero-dimensional local blocks; Weil restrictions of low-dimensional algebraic sets are semi-local. A summation polynomial S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m, c) defines a positive-dimensional set, so the theorem does not apply to it before the factor-base and field equations are imposed.
assumptions: Each local block zero-dimensional and radical

nodes.label: Petit-Quisquater: first fall degree of descended S_{m+1} <= m^2 + 1
nodes.statement: For the Weil descent over F_{2^n} of Semaev's (m+1)-th summation polynomial with an n'-dimensional factor-base subspace, the first fall degree is at most m^2 + 1; with m = n^{1/3} this is n^{2/3} + 1 (Petit-Quisquater Proposition 1; the m^2 + 1 bound also follows from Hodges-Petit-Schlather Theorem 5.2).
nodes.scope: Not read here; taken from Kousidis-Wiemers Section 3 and Section 4. A first-fall bound, so it is a cost bound only through Assumption 2.
source_locations: Petit-Quisquater 2012, Proposition 1 and Section 4 (via Kousidis-Wiemers 2019, Sections 1, 3, 4)

nodes.label: Kousidis-Wiemers: first fall degree of descended S_{m+1} <= m^2 - m + 1
nodes.statement: For n' >= m >= 3 and c in F_{2^n} \ {0}, the Boolean system s_0..s_{n-1} from the Weil descent of S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m, c) (over F_2[y]/(y^2 - y)) has first fall degree (Hodges-Petit-Schlather Definition 2.2) at most m^2 - m + 1, because its highest-degree homogeneous part has degree m^2 - m (Lemma 3.1). For m = 2 the bound reads 3 but the true value is 2 (Kosters-Yeo).
nodes.scope: Rigorous upper bound on a first fall degree; says nothing about the solving degree. The authors believe it sharp for m >= 3.
assumptions: First fall degree in the HPS filtered-algebra sense

nodes.label: Kousidis-Wiemers Table 1: D_ff = 2 but D_reg rises to 5 for m = 2; equal for small m = 3, 4
nodes.statement: Magma GroebnerBasis on Weil descents of S_{m+1} over F_{2^n} with random curves, random n' = ceil(n/m)-dimensional factor-base subspaces, 10 repetitions per cell: m = 2, n = 34..48: D_ff = 2 always, D_reg (highest step degree) = 4 for n <= 36 and 5 for n = 37..48 (memory up to 208 GB at n = 48); m = 3, n = 13..21: D_ff = D_reg = 7; m = 4, n = 13..16: D_ff = D_reg = 13. With the low-degree basis span{1, z, .., z^{n'}} the rise for m = 2 appears at n = 45.
nodes.scope: Empirical first fall = Magma step degree of the first degree fall; D_reg = highest step degree (a solving-degree proxy). For m >= 3 only small n are covered, so the equality there says nothing about growth. The authors state that such data can neither falsify Petit-Quisquater Assumption 2 nor confirm n-dependence.

nodes.label: Petit-Quisquater Assumption 2: D_reg = D_ff + o(1) for binary summation descents
nodes.statement: The degree of regularity (maximal degree reached) of the Weil-descended summation-polynomial system equals its first fall degree up to o(1) as n grows; Kousidis-Wiemers rephrase it as the open question D_reg = m^2 - m + 1 + o(1).
nodes.scope: The specific heuristic behind the binary-field subexponential ECDLP claims (a special case of HEUR-FIRST-FALL-DEGREE). Contradicted at m = 2 by the n-dependence of D_reg with D_ff fixed at 2 (Kosters-Yeo; KW Table 1); HKY 2015 report computational evidence against it and construct a descent system where it is unlikely to hold; CG 2021 Section 4 shows first fall and solving degree are unrelated in general.
assumptions: The first degree fall controls the whole computation
failure_modes: D_reg grows with n while D_ff is constant (observed at m = 2)
First fall exhibited by low-degree structure unrelated to the solution (CG 2021 Ex. 4.2, 4.4)

cited_by.note: GbStats records the maximal degree reached on descended PQ systems against the first-fall bound
reproduces the shape of Petit-Quisquater Table 2 (degree reached vs derived bound)

nodes.label: Petit-Quisquater subexponential binary ECDLP: 2^{c n^{2/3} log n}
nodes.statement: Under Assumption 2, index calculus with Weil-descended summation polynomials solves ECDLP over F_{2^n} in O(2^{c n^{2/3} log n}) with c = 2 omega/3, choosing m = n^{1/3} (Petit-Quisquater Proposition 4), beating generic O(2^{n/2}) for n >= about 2000; with the Kousidis-Wiemers first-fall bound assumed sharp the exponent becomes c log(n) (n^{2/3} - n^{1/3} + 1) and the crossover about 1250.
nodes.scope: Conditional on Assumption 2 and on relation-probability heuristics; crossovers are far above cryptographic n (<= 521, as KW note). Not a bound on any concrete curve.
assumptions: Decomposition probability and relation rank heuristics
source_locations: Petit-Quisquater 2012, Proposition 4 and Section 5 (via Kousidis-Wiemers 2019, eq. (4.2))

nodes.label: Hodges-Petit-Schlather: first fall degree bounds for Weil descent
nodes.statement: Defines the first fall degree of a system in the filtered algebra F_{2^n}[X]/(X_i^2 - X_i) (Definitions 2.1-2.2; invariant under base-field extension, Corollary 2.4) and bounds it for Weil-descent systems; Theorem 4.9 (as quoted by HMS Thm 4.7): a homogeneous element of degree d > 1 and rank s has D_ff <= (s + d + 2)/2; Theorem 5.2 yields the m^2 + 1 bound for descended summation polynomials (as used by KW).
nodes.scope: Not read (repository download refused). Bounds a first fall degree only.
source_locations: Hodges-Petit-Schlather 2014, Definitions 2.1, 2.2, Corollary 2.4, Theorem 4.9, Theorem 5.2 (via HMS 2017 Thm 4.7 and Kousidis-Wiemers 2019)

nodes.label: HKY 2015: computational evidence against the first fall degree assumption for ECDLP
nodes.statement: Huang-Kosters-Yeo (CRYPTO 2015) present computational evidence that casts doubt on the first fall degree assumption used for subexponential characteristic-2 ECDLP claims, construct a Weil descent system from summation polynomials for which the assumption is unlikely to hold, and conclude that complexity estimates resting on it need more care; they also prove HFE systems have small last fall degree (unconditional polynomial time for fixed defining degree and base field).
nodes.scope: Abstract-level only (ePrint 2015/573 metadata; PDF not read). HKYY (read) confirm the context: 'more recent works ... have cast serious doubt on the first fall degree assumption' and summation descents without field equations are not zero-dimensional.

nodes.label: First-fall/degree-of-regularity HFE estimates (Dubois-Gama, Ding-Hodges, Ding-Kleinjung)
nodes.statement: Dubois-Gama bound the (first-fall) degree of regularity of HFE systems; Ding-Hodges claim inverting HFE is quasi-polynomial for all fields, relying on 'the standard assumption that the Groebner basis algorithms terminate at or shortly after the degree of regularity', where their degree of regularity is a first fall degree; Ding-Kleinjung bound it for HFE- and estimate about 2^97 for HFE Challenge 2.
nodes.scope: Conditional on the first-fall-to-solver step. Later rigorous work replaced these with proved last-fall (HKY15/HKYY, GMP Thm 11) and solving-degree (GMP Thm 5) bounds for HFE. Recorded because the same first-fall technique was transplanted to summation-polynomial ECDLP.
assumptions: First fall degree approximates the solving degree

nodes.label: Ding-Schmidt 2013: degenerate systems with first-fall degree far below the solving degree
nodes.statement: Ding and Schmidt show that the Dubois-Gama/Ding-Schmidt degree of regularity (first fall degree) and the solving degree of quadratic systems over finite fields need not be close: 'degenerate' systems where they are far apart are easy to produce.
nodes.scope: Not read; reported by Caminata-Gorla 2020 Section 4.2 and Caminata-Gorla 2021 Section 4.

nodes.label: Does the solving degree of binary summation descents grow with n?
nodes.statement: Open: for the Weil descent over F_{2^n} of S_{m+1} with a factor-base subspace (with field equations), is the solving degree (or last fall degree) bounded independently of n for fixed m (Kousidis-Wiemers question (4.1): D_reg = m^2 - m + 1 + o(1)?), or does it grow (as observed at m = 2: 4 -> 5 between n = 36 and 37)?
nodes.scope: No rigorous bound independent of n exists: HKYY's n-independent last fall needs zero-dimensionality of the system over F_{2^n}, CCG bounds grow linearly in n, Huang 2021/2023 bound only linearized or zero-dimensional semi-local parts. This is the open step under every subexponential binary-field estimate.

edges.statement: Remark 15 bounds maxGBdeg by d_reg.

The heuristic predicts cost at the BFS d_reg.

HFE estimates bound this first-fall-type degree of regularity.
Asymptotics hold for semi-regular sequences.
Bounds hypothesise cryptographic semi-regularity of F or F^h.
Pardue: Froberg's conjecture is equivalent to generic sequences being semi-regular.
The conjecture is about semi-regularity over F_2.

Steiner characterises generic coordinates.

Supplies a rigorous D (sum (d_i-1)+1) for regular/generic systems to insert in Proposition 1.

The heuristic plugs these asymptotic d_reg values into the cost.
